body:
## Problem

Inside a container, dss reports files in **image (lower) layers** as reclaimable, although deleting them frees **0 bytes** on the host: overlayfs only records a whiteout. In our case the image is a `docker commit` snapshot of a crashed task (`start-command-resume/<name>:N`), so the "reclaimable" bytes are frozen in that image while the task runs.

Environment: dss 0.14.1 from `main` (`0c4a695`, run from source with `node bin/dss.js`; npm still has 0.13.1, #19). Host: Ubuntu 24.04, Docker 29.6.1 with the containerd image store. Inside: hive-mind DinD task containers (`konard/hive-mind-dind:2.34.0`, user `box` uid 1001, an inner root `dockerd`), resumed from `docker commit` snapshots after a host dockerd crash. All runs were `scan --no-docker --json --tier moderate` (never deletes) with `DOCKER_HOST=unix:///nonexistent.sock` (#22).

| Task container | writable layer (`ctr -n moby snapshots --snapshotter overlayfs usage <id>`) | dss "safe", unblocked |
|---|---|---|
| router#727 (`175ff931…-resume-1`, run as root, see the liveness issue) | **345.4 MiB** | **13.79 GiB** |
| router#724 (`9243e682…-resume-1-resume-2`) | **5.9 GiB** | **16.41 GiB** |

The biggest items in both are `cargo-superseded-leaf` (9.37 / 11.44 GiB) in the pre-crash work dir `/tmp/gh-issue-solver-<ts>/target/debug` and `bun-cache` (2.30 / 2.73 GiB). They all date from before the snapshot. A `dss clean` would delete about 14 GiB, free nothing on the host, and take caches away from the running task. Only removing the task's snapshot images after it finishes returns that space.

This is item 4 of #14 ("image-layer caches counted as reclaimable"), which was closed. It still reproduces on `main` for in-container scans.

## Suggested fix

- **From the host / outer daemon (best data, and fast):** measure each container's writable layer directly: containerd snapshotter `ctr -n moby snapshots --snapshotter overlayfs usage <container-id>` (milliseconds), overlay2 `docker inspect -f '{{.GraphDriver.Data.UpperDir}}'` + `du`. Walk the **upperdir** to list what is actually freeable per path. This also replaces the slow `docker diff` measurement of #21, and the `docker diff` storm of #22.
- **From inside a container** (no host access): detect an overlay root in `/proc/self/mountinfo`. If it is overlay, report candidate bytes as "may be in an image layer, freeable bytes unknown" and leave them out of the reclaimable total, unless an outer dss passed per-path upperdir sizes down.
- In the report, show image-layer bytes separately as "0 B freeable now (in image <ref>; freed when the container and image are removed)". For `start-command-resume/*` images, point to removing the container and image after the task completes.
- Test: an overlay fixture where the lower layer holds a cache dir must report 0 B freeable for it.

---

We need to download all logs and data related about the issue to this repository, make sure we compile that data to `./docs/case-studies/issue-{id}` folder, and use it to do deep case study analysis (also make sure to search online for additional facts and data), in which we will reconstruct timeline/sequence of events, list of each and all requirements from the issue, find root causes of the each problem, and propose possible solutions and solution plans for each requirement (we should also check known existing components/libraries, that solve similar problem or can help in solutions).

If there is not enough data to find actual root cause, add debug output and verbose mode if not present, that will allow us to find root cause on next iteration.

If issue related to any other repository/project, where we can report issues on GitHub, please do so. Each issue must contain reproducible examples, workarounds and suggestions for fix the issue in code. Also double check to fully apply requirements to entire codebase, so if we have issue in multiple places, it should be fixed in all them.

Please plan and execute everything in this single pull request, you have unlimited time and context, as context auto-compacts and you can continue indefinitely, until it is each and every requirement fully addressed, and everything is totally done.
title: In-container scan still counts image-layer bytes as reclaimable: 13.79 GiB "safe" in a container whose writable layer is 345 MiB (#14 item 4)
